result:
All six defects fixed and `submission.md` updated.

## The three major ones (all R9)

I re-derived each from my own extraction before touching the text; all three reproduce exactly as reported.

**[1.1]** "the sole empirical support **anywhere**" was false — Denning's §2 invokes Fine et al. and Varian & Coffman's experiments twice and Belady's comparison. Narrowed to what the argument actually needs: he leans on measurement elsewhere, but *the ranking* rests on one sentence of the conclusion.

**[1.2]** The Mach quote was cut exactly where the paper supplies its justification ("…that Mach is able to outperform a version of UNIX (IBM ACIS 4.2a) on the RT"). Rewritten to name that justification and say why it's weak — which, as you pointed out, ties back to my own first critique paragraph and makes the point stronger: the ACIS result is another end-to-end win that no more separates `pmap`'s cost than the fork figures do.

**[1.3]** "and then leaves it there" — the phrasing R9 names explicitly. §3.5 garbage-collects shadow objects and the next sentence carries into the locking rules. You were right that `submission.md` described the correct framing while `answer.tex` shipped the opposite; the analysis was right and the prose didn't match it. Now it does.

## The minor ones

Quote de-capitalised to the abstract's wording, τ stated as "comparable to T" with 2T as the 50%-tolerance value, and the 60% worst case restored to the SHA-1 rejection basis.

**[1.4] was the one worth fixing properly.** A verifier holding a hardcoded copy of a quotation cannot catch the quotation drifting — that's a process failure, not a wording one. `verify_quotes.py` now parses the quotations out of `answer.tex`, so what gets checked is always what ships. It immediately found that Denning's *title* doesn't appear contiguously (the scan splits it across the column gutter), so titles are matched word-in-order and prose quotes contiguously. 11/11, exit 0. The rewritten script would have failed round 1.

## Length — disclosed, not spun

1542 words, up from 1464. The fixes added 117: replacing an asserted absence with what the paper does next is strictly more text than the false shorter version. A trim pass took 1581 back to 1542, and I stopped — what remains is quotes, section numbers and table values, and cutting further would remove the anchoring the R9 fixes exist to supply. Still inside R8's threshold (1688), but the direction is wrong and I've said so in `submission.md`, along with which paragraph to cut first if you want it shorter.

One process note: my round-1 PNGs went stale mid-session and I read the pre-trim render once before catching it. I re-rendered and read all three pages against the shipped file.

Compile exit 0, zero warnings, zero over/underfull boxes, 3 pages. Lint exit 0.
